purpose: Runs Squire's one-off set-up against a loopback stand-in of Cloudflare's API and reads the account back through it, to check paid features, anything the set-up cannot read as free, the spend guard and the removal of the set-up token; the real one-off set-up, against a test Cloudflare account and never a live one, is the test stage's own step.
title: Safe Cloudflare set-up

testCases.description: after set-up no paid subscription, only the deploy-only token left and the set-up token gone
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::after the one-off set-up, the account read back shows no paid subscription, the only token left on it deploys and nothing else, so nothing left there can spend, and the set-up token is gone; a paid subscription found on stops the set-up, which names it and changes no billing; a set-up token without the rights it needs runs nothing

testCases.description: the set-up token is removed even when a later step fails, and the owner is told what was left
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::the set-up token is removed from the account even when a later step of the set-up fails, and a set-up that did not finish tells the owner what it left on the account: making the deploy token fails, or its first use fails

testCases.description: the set-up token reaches the set-up only through the secret helper and is never written anywhere
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::the set-up token reaches the set-up only through Squire's secret helper, from the Keychain, and is never written to a file, the chat or the ledger; a set-up token given any other way, or a Cloudflare token already on the Mac, is never used

testCases.description: a call that would upgrade a plan or buy on the account is refused, yes or no
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::Squire never upgrades a plan or buys on the Cloudflare account: a call to Cloudflare's API that would is refused, not asked, yes or no, in the default mode and in auto mode, by curl or through Squire's secret helper with the deploy token

testCases.description: a subscription the set-up cannot read as free counts as paid: named with its price, warned of, and kept only on the owner's yes
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::a subscription the set-up cannot read as free counts as paid: the set-up names it with its price, or says it cannot read the price, warns that it costs money and that Squire changes no billing, and does not report done; on the owner's yes to keeping it, asked naming it in the default mode and in auto mode, the set-up finishes, keeps one deploy-only token and names it in its done words; when it cannot read the subscriptions at all it does not report done and says so

testCases.description: a set-up token whose removal fails is named, and the set-up does not report done
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::when the set-up cannot remove its own set-up token from the account, it does not report done and names the set-up token to the owner as still on the account, names every other token it left there, and keeps nothing in the Keychain

testCases.description: a paid-plan write by a client other than curl is refused, yes or no
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::Squire never buys on the Cloudflare account by a client other than curl: the same paid-plan write to the account's subscriptions by wget or by a python3 urllib call is refused, not asked, yes or no, the refusal saying it is about money, in the default mode and in auto mode

testCases.description: a browser navigate to the Cloudflare dashboard is refused, yes or no
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::Squire's browser never opens the Cloudflare dashboard, where a plan could be bought: in a site job, with the owner's profile there to check, a browser navigate to the dashboard's host is refused, not asked, yes or no, the refusal naming the dashboard or money, in the default mode and in auto mode

testCases.description: a user-owned set-up token gets words that it must be account-owned and where to make it
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::a set-up token the owner made under their own profile, which Cloudflare refuses on the account's path and accepts on the user path, gets words that say the set-up token must be an account-owned token, made under Manage account, then Account API Tokens; the set-up makes nothing on the account and keeps nothing in the Keychain

testCases.description: a token refused on both paths keeps today's words and is never called user-owned
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::a set-up token Cloudflare refuses on both the account's path and the user path keeps today's words, to check the account id and the token, and is never called user-owned or sent to make an account-owned one; the set-up makes nothing and keeps nothing

testCases.description: a user-owned set-up token the account's path refuses another way, and the user path accepts, gets the account-owned words and where to make one; nothing made, nothing kept
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::a set-up token Cloudflare refuses on the account's path with another refusal than an invalid token, and accepts on the user path, gets words that say the set-up token must be an account-owned token, made under Manage account, then Account API Tokens; the set-up makes nothing on the account and keeps nothing in the Keychain

testCases.description: a set-up token refused another way on the account's path and refused on the user path too keeps today's words and is never called user-owned; nothing made, nothing kept
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::a set-up token Cloudflare refuses on the account's path with another refusal than an invalid token, and refuses on the user path too, keeps today's words, to check the account id and the token, and is never called user-owned or sent to make an account-owned one; the set-up makes nothing and keeps nothing

testCases.description: with a paid item and no yes or a no the set-up does not report done; a yes covers only the paid items named before it
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::with a paid item named and no yes, or a no, the set-up does not report done and keeps nothing: the owner's no to keeping it, asked in the default mode and in auto mode, keeps that run from going ahead; a yes to an ordinary run of the set-up is not a yes to keeping it; and a yes covers only the paid items named before it, so one found after it is named and the set-up does not report done

testCases.description: a paid item on the second page of subscriptions is found, named with its price and asked
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/website-set-up.test.js::a paid item on the second page of the account's subscriptions is found, named with its price and asked: with the first page free and the answer naming a second, the set-up reads every page, does not report done before the owner's yes, and on his yes to keeping it, asked naming it in the default mode and in auto mode, finishes naming it
